newsitem.title: USA: Plastic surgeon found guilty of aiding drug dealer.
newsitem.headline: Plastic surgeon found guilty of aiding drug dealer.

text.p: A plastic surgeon was convicted on Thursday of using his skills to alter the appearance of a wanted drug dealer, officials said.
Dr. Jose Castillo, 63, faced a mandatory minimum five-year prison sentence on federal charges of harbouring a fugitive and obstructing justice.

The trial began on Feb. 18. On Thursday the jury concluded that Castillo had performed plastic surgery on Richard Ramos after Ramos was indicted in September 1990 as the ringleader of a notorious cocaine ring in Philadelphia.
Assistant U.S. Attorney Kristen Hayes said Ramos eluded arrest for years. She said he was caught in 1995 while visiting his family in Philadelphia, by federal agents acting on a tip.

The agents said the plastic surgery -- including removal of fat from Ramos' cheeks and jawline, narrowing his nose and reducing the appearance of scars -- had altered Ramos' appearance so much that they did not recognise him.
In addition, in an effort to change Ramos' fingerprints, Castillo injected collagen into the fugitive's fingertips, Hayes said.
Castillo's defence lawyers said the doctor did not know his patient had legal problems and thought he was repairing scars from a backyard barbecue accident.

The doctor's defence was that he performed the surgery in May 1990, before Ramos was indicted. However, police officers testified that they interviewed Ramos a week after Castillo said he had performed the surgery and noticed no change in his appearance.
Ramos and dozens of accomplices are serving federal prison terms for drug dealing. Ramos testified against Castillo, but when asked, he failed to identify him in the courtroom.
